Ground Water
Westmoreland Resources has established a network of test wells for the purpose of determining baseline hydrologic conditions. The system includes five groups of wells on Tract II and nine groups of wells on Tract III. Various aspects of the one-year baseline study will be complete in the spring and summer of 1976, at which time Westmoreland Resources will implement a monitoring program designed to detect changes in ground water quantity and quality. The details of the program will be finalized in consultation with the Montana Department of State Lands. Westmoreland Resources anticipates that the monitoring program will consist of monthly measurement of water levels and annual water quality sampling in Tract III wells. A similar program will be implemented on Tract II at the time mining operations are initiated (David W. Simpson, Westmoreland Resources, personal comm.).
Montana law requires that a mine operator replace water supplies lost or degraded as a result of mining. Any such loss from a shallow aquifer will be replaced by drilling a well to the sub-Robinson unit, which will not be affected by mining.
The effects of leaching on ground water will be minimized by diverting surface water around areas involved in active mining. This water will be channeled into the internal drainage system. Prompt revegetation will minimize leaching in reclaimed areas.
